assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential empirical and conceptual account of how trade, technology and tasks reshape labour demand and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson provide a coherent core for the trade-shock and task-based evidence; related contributors make exact boundaries necessarily contestable.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda has been extensively tested, replicated and incorporated into labour and trade research and public-policy debate.
uncertainties: The relative importance of trade, automation and institutions varies across settings.
Lawrence F. Katz is also a major contributor to portions of the broader agenda.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data research has transformed measurement and explanation of intergenerational mobility and its geographic variation.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the mobility program, with Friedman a major collaborator in its foundational data and measurement work.
assessment.maturity: The findings have generated a durable research infrastructure, broad scholarly use and substantial policy relevance.
uncertainties: Interpretation of geographic mobility differences remains contested.
The contribution is distributed across a large collaborative research program.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs made discrimination in labour markets observable with unusually clear causal evidence.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are especially closely associated with landmark correspondence-study evidence; the field has many important precursors and extensions.
assessment.maturity: The approach is established across countries and markets and has reshaped empirical research on discrimination.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates identify important mechanisms but do not exhaust all forms of labour-market discrimination.
Credit allocation among foundational field-experiment contributors is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods supplied a widely applicable solution to persistent endogeneity and unobserved heterogeneity in panel data.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond form a natural attribution group for the core estimators and their development.
assessment.maturity: These methods are longstanding standards in applied microeconometrics, with well-understood diagnostics and limitations.
uncertainties: Weak-instrument and finite-sample problems limit automatic application.
The broader GMM tradition has numerous antecedents.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern monopsony framework has fundamentally altered analysis of wages, employer power and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning is a central architect of the modern analytical framework, although subsequent empirical work is broadly dispersed.
assessment.maturity: The framework now motivates extensive empirical measurement and has major consequences for minimum-wage and antitrust policy.
uncertainties: Empirical magnitudes of employer power differ considerably by market and design.
Credit for the empirical revival extends beyond the named group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life health, shocks and skill formation has demonstrated the large, persistent economic consequences of childhood conditions.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond and Cunha represent complementary empirical and theoretical contributions to this influential literature.
assessment.maturity: Evidence from multiple cohorts, shocks and administrative-data settings has made early-life conditions a durable field of inquiry.
uncertainties: Causal mechanisms and the scope for remediation remain context-dependent.
The agenda includes many other essential contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection supplied a powerful explanation of trade patterns, reallocation and aggregate gains from trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is indispensable to the canonical model, while Helpman and Redding are leading contributors to its theoretical and empirical development.
assessment.maturity: The framework is a central, extensively used part of modern international-trade analysis.
uncertainties: Quantitative welfare implications depend on model structure and empirical implementation.
Attribution across the broader heterogeneous-firm trade literature is not uniquely determined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed econometric practice by making transparent what data can support under credible, limited assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the foundational figure in partial identification, and Tamer made major contributions to moment-inequality methods.
assessment.maturity: The approach is theoretically mature and increasingly consequential wherever point identification is implausible.
uncertainties: Its applied uptake remains less uniform than that of conventional point-estimation methods.
The appropriate degree of identifying restriction is application-specific.
